It’s a warm experience as the weather chills.
It’s a loosely familiar tale of time travel, based on a short story written by Hanks that tries, and half-succeeds, to bring something new to a table we’ve sat at many times before.
“This World of Tomorrow” shares with its co-author and star an easygoing wholesomeness, but its anodyne nature becomes a liability as it stretches to two acts.
But "This World of Tomorrow" is not a classic—it's a clunker.
In a hundred years, scientists could study how his new play, a befuddling sci-fi rom-com playing off-Broadway at the Shed, became one of the more inane star vehicles of our time.
Whether a theater company should spend its time and resources developing and staging what he has written is another question.
This is a show worth traveling from any century for.
And somedays a disappointing play worth sitting through for some superior acting.
“This World of Tomorrow,” which opened tonight at The Shed, is as old-fashioned as they come, like an overlong episode of an awkward early 1950s TV series.
Still, we can’t shake the feeling that This World of Tomorrow would be better off as a movie.
Their combined star power makes This World of Tomorrow a must-see event, even if you never shake the feeling that it would have worked much better as a film.
Alas, charming as it often is, This World of Tomorrow feels very yesterday.
But as an attempt to wed the two genres of time travel and romantic comedy without having anything new to say about either is rather disappointing.

This World of Tomorrow may not dazzle with spectacle or narrative urgency, but it does offer something unique: a sincere meditation on memory, longing, and the enduring hope that love, like time, might still bend in our favour.
Tom Hanks brings undeniable star power to this time travel romance, but the play never quite takes off.
A catatonic dullness and brace of stereotypical side characters further clog the pacing of This World of Tomorrow.
Despite the sci-fi trappings, This World of Tomorrow is stuck in the dusty past, a time dripping in sentimentality and the possibility of a whirlwind romance with a person you only just met.
Dede Ayite’s costumes help differentiate the various time periods, but it still feels like multiple stories unsuccessfully merged into one.

cn.t: Critics find Hanks' nostalgic time-travel romance well-intentioned but slight and overextended, with praise for co-star Kelli O'Hara but concerns about pacing and depth. Reception ranges from charming to dull.

vr.q: While I wouldn't call this riveting theatre, I enjoyed it for what it is, and I can see the target audience getting a decent kick out of it.
